title: Edge API triage notes: timeouts, 429s, streaming degradation
summary: Informal SRE runbook sketch for triage and quick mitigations when the edge API shows client timeouts, spikes of 429 responses, degraded streaming behavior, or elevated 5xx error rates. Intended for on-call engineers to use as an immediate checklist prior to a full incident writeup.
scope: Applies to Redwood hosted inference public API ingress path (edge LB -> api-gateway -> model-proxy -> model workers). Focus is on 0-2 hour triage actions and safe short-term mitigations.
owners: Primary: Maya Chen; Secondary: Asha Patel; Escalation: Diego Ramirez
quick_indicators: Sudden increase in gateway 502/504 and overall p99 latency
Spike in 429 count grouped by client_id or route
Stream chunk rate drops or last-chunk-time increases
Backend model workers show high queue depth and CPU/GPU utilization
initial_triage_steps: Acknowledge alert and start incident note (include who, what, time, scope)
Verify detection signal(s) on SLO dashboard and list top three symptoms
Run topk error queries to identify affected routes/models/clients
Check k8s pods for CrashLoopBackOff or OOM and node pressure
Scan gateway and model-server logs for correlated error messages or trace IDs
If streaming: inspect per-connection last-chunk timestamps and backlog metrics
quick_mitigations: Temporarily raise per-client rate limits for affected customers via feature flag
Scale up model-serving replicas or spin new pool for the affected model
Cordon and drain problematic nodes showing OOMs; use autoscaler to replace
Split traffic to a lighter/fallback model variant or cached responses
Route traffic away from problematic region(s) to healthy regions
For streaming stalls, consider toggling proxy chunking behavior or increase proxy timeouts briefly
investigation_queries_and_dashboards: Histogram: stream_chunk_latency_seconds by model and connection
Per-model inference_latency_seconds p50/p95/p99 and queue depth metrics
common_failure_patterns_and_actions: Client timeouts: pattern = upstream queuing causing high tail latency. Actions: increase replicas, enable caching for repeated prompts, cap input tokens, route to quantized/smaller model variant.

429 storms: pattern = traffic spike or internal retry loop. Actions: identify top offenders, enable soft-burst overrides for trusted clients, deploy Retry-After headers, rollback offending deploy if internal.

Degraded streaming: pattern = generation stalls or continuous-batching tail. Actions: check model runtime for stuck sampling loops, disable continuous batching for model, restart worker replicas, revert proxy config changes.

Elevated 5xx: pattern = OOMs, model load errors, networking failures. Actions: inspect model-server stack traces, rollback recent model/infra deploys, increase model load timeouts or pre-warm models, apply circuit-breaker to non-critical routes.
oncall_playbook_snippets: kubectl logs deploy/api-gateway -c gateway --since=15m | jq -r '.route' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
observability_gaps: No reliable per-connection streaming health metric (bytes/sec, last-chunk-time) emitted by runtime
Missing alert for sustained p99 stream_chunk_latency > 3s
Trace-id propagation not consistent between gateway and model-server logs
No automated safe-unpublish for repeatedly failing model loads
post_incident_checklist: Build timeline with timestamps and deploy IDs for all services
Collect representative traces, attach trace IDs and logs
Map recent config or code changes in 2 hours before incident and correlate to failures
Create action items with owners and deadlines for telemetry fixes and permanent mitigations
notes_to_self: Prototype a graceful-degrade API mode to reduce model size for new requests when SLOs breach
Investigate per-tenant adaptive rate limiting that auto-lifts when cache hits available
Schedule chaos tests targeting streaming chunk delays to validate recovery behavior
